content.thinking:
I'm drafting the spec and settling the order: decline, escalate, request_docs, incomplete, then approve, with the order citing section 2.1. For the unknown-facts case, I'll cite section 2.2 for the rule that a case with an unknown required fact can't be approved, and then mark it as incomplete.

I'm working out which people count as identified individuals for the collection rules: the control person and anyone owning 25% or more, with the open question being whether the agent's listing or a certified ownership percentage should change that.

I'm working out the counting rule for identified individuals: the control person always counts, and so does any owner at 25% or more, but only when the entity isn't excluded. Nonprofits still get their control person identified, just not their owners, so I'll account for that split.

I'm weighing whether the agent's "listed" flag should count toward identified individuals, or whether only the control person and owners at 25% or more should, and I'm leaning toward the SOP's own definition, which covers only those two groups.

I'm checking whether shares held through an excluded entity below 25% still have to be traced to individuals, since those shares wouldn't be in the unaccounted total.

I'm checking whether shares held through an excluded entity below 25% should count as open for completeness, since the pack doesn't trace them further up. If so, I'd add those shares to the unaccounted total and request documents when the combined open percentage reaches 25.

I'm checking whether a person who isn't formally identified could still reach 25% when their known share is combined with the open percentage, which would make ownership incomplete and call for documents.

I'm reconsidering whether a known person below 25% could still reach 25% once the unaccounted share is added, and I'm weighing whether a listed 25%-plus owner who wasn't flagged as listed should count as a failure to identify under section 3.3.

I'm now weighing whether a person who isn't flagged as listed should still count, and I'm leaning toward not requiring the flag, since the case data already names them. Whether someone known at 30% but unlisted should drive a completeness failure is still open for me, so I'll decide that after checking section 3.3's wording.

I'm settling how an empty list of identified individuals should be handled: an excluded entity needs no one identified, so that case gets an explicit allowance, while a non-excluded entity with no control person or 25% owner in the list shouldn't just fall through to unknown.

I'm now settling the rule for which entity types need identified individuals, and I'm checking how the excluded-list case should be allowed for an empty list. Then I'll note that 3.2 and 3.3 both apply to the collection, so it needs references to both.

I'm settling the collection's wording: the excluded-list sentence, the control-person sentence, and the 25%-owner sentence, citing sections 3.1 through 3.3. I'm also deciding whether the excluded-owners list needs a counting rule, since it may not.

I'm settling the computed open-percentage rule: the unaccounted share plus any excluded-owner shares still under 25%, and I'm holding off on writing out the ownership-completeness sentence until I've checked whether an excluded entity's share can be left out of it.

I'm checking whether an excluded entity's shares below 25% still count as open, since the SOP only exempts shares of 25% or more, so those would need individuals identified and would feed into the open percentage.

I'm dropping the partial-ownership rule, since "some" only looks at items that count as identified, and a sub-25% person who counts is a control person who is already identified, so that rule can't apply.

I'm adding the registry-age check: if the entity's filing is under 12 months old, documents have to be requested. I'm also setting aside the over-allocation fact, since the SOP doesn't reference it, and I'm confirming that unknown exclusion status keeps the 3.3 rule open to being triggered, which leads to incomplete.

I'm setting the sanctions rules next: a confirmed match on the entity or any identified individual means decline, and a potential match that hasn't been cleared means escalate. I'm also adding escalation for a PEP among identified individuals and for adverse media on the entity or those individuals, leaving the materiality bar to the fact's definition.

I'm weighing whether to list the recording requirement for searches as a need, since the SOP attaches no outcome to it, and I'm leaning toward noting it in the section rather than adding a rule.

I'm mapping the industry names to their categories, with the SOP's prohibited terms and the msb and crypto variants, and I'm keeping the list to those wordings for now.

I'm adding normal-industry mappings for common business types like software, retail, and consulting, since without them every ordinary business would stay unresolved and end up incomplete.

I'm adding a normal-industry mapping for cryptocurrency-adjacent wording, treating "crypto" and "cryptocurrency" as the crypto category and "money transmitter" as msb, and I'm listing "cannabis" alongside "marijuana-related business" as prohibited.

I'm settling the industry mappings now: the SOP's prohibited terms and msb and crypto variants, plus a few cannabis and adult-entertainment wordings. I'm also weighing the 5.3 licensed-MSB permission against the 5.2 escalation, since the order puts escalate ahead of approve, which means the permission would never decide the outcome.

I'm settling on an approve default: section 1 says approve when everything is met and no risk applies, so I'll write it as a rule that always holds, since the earlier outcomes already catch the cases that should stop it.

I'm settling the approve outcome, with 5.3 as its own approve rule for verified-licence money services businesses, so the conflict with 5.2 stays visible rather than being smoothed over. I'm also considering whether verified licence should exempt those businesses from the escalation, but that would be changing the rule rather than writing it as stated, so I'm leaving it alone and checking the phrase about unlicensed money transmission next.

I'm treating the 5.2 escalation as the rule that wins over the 5.3 approval for verified money services businesses, and I'll leave the mismatch visible rather than fixing it. For the section 1 items, the incomplete outcome covers any required fact that hasn't been established.

I'm checking the registry-age and trust-share handling in the remaining sections, and noting that the sanctions outcomes are straightforward: a sanctioned country or a sanctioned resident means decline, and a high-risk jurisdiction means escalate.

I'm checking whether an excluded entity's control person needs to count as identified when that person is named in the case, since the SOP's sanctions rule covers any identified individual, and I'm weighing whether the agent's listing should bring them in.

I'm checking the open-percentage formula: the unaccounted share plus any excluded-owner shares still under 25%, and I'm confirming the per-item condition sits inside the sum. Then I'm double-checking the wording of the approve-by-label line.

I'm settling the exact wording for the approve default, the unknown-facts sentence, and the control-person and 25%-owner collection rules, all citing their sections.

I'm writing out the wording for the collection rules, pulling in the rule that a non-excluded entity needs ownership completeness checked against unaccounted shares and shares held through entities with unknown owners. I'm also setting the prohibited-industry wording for decline, covering marijuana-related business, adult content, and unlicensed money transmission, and checking whether the record-searches requirement needs any outcome of its own.

I'm drafting the output rules now: the default approve rule will be an empty all-condition, and I'm writing the collection entries with their counts_when, empty_ok_when, unknown_when_empty, sop and text fields. I'm also deciding whether to include a need about separating unlicensed from unverified licences, leaning toward keeping the needs list to the record-searches item.

unknowns.text: If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the case cannot be approved.

people.unknown_when_empty: who the identified individuals are (the control person and every individual owning 25% or more)
people.text: Entities on the excluded list do not require beneficial owners to be identified. ... For every other entity, identify one control person: a single individual with significant responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity. ... Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly.

computed.text: Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share.

rules.text: For every other entity, identify one control person: a single individual with significant responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity. If no control person is identified, request documents.

Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly. Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share. If ownership is not complete, request documents.
Verify the identity of every identified individual. If any is unverified, request documents.
The entity's registry filing must be less than 12 months old. Otherwise request documents.
A confirmed sanctions match on the entity or any identified individual: decline.
A potential sanctions match that has not been cleared: escalate.
A politically exposed person among the identified individuals: escalate.
Adverse media on the entity or any identified individual: escalate.
Prohibited industries (marijuana-related business, adult content, unlicensed money transmission): decline.
Restricted industries (money services businesses, virtual currency): escalate.
Licensed money services businesses whose state licence has been verified may be approved.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a comprehensively sanctioned country: decline.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a FATF high-risk or increased-monitoring jurisdiction: escalate.
all requirements below are met and no risk factor applies.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes. Approve is the last outcome in the order and applies when nothing more severe does. Incomplete is the unknowns outcome.
Sets `order`: decline, escalate, request_docs, incomplete, approve.
Sets `unknowns`. A rule that might apply because of an unknown fact leads to incomplete, so the case is not approved.

This is an exemption, not an outcome. It is used as `excluded` = no in rules control-person-missing and ownership-incomplete, in the people list's `counts_when`, and as the people list's `empty_ok_when`.
Also defines identified individuals: the control person is one, unless the entity is excluded (people `counts_when`).

The computed fact open_pct adds unaccounted_pct to the shares held through excluded entities that own less than 25%. Only an excluded entity owning 25% or more is exempt. Owners of 25% or more are identified individuals unless the entity is excluded or a nonprofit (people `counts_when`). An unidentified person who is already named with a smaller share could also reach 25% when combined with open shares. That case cannot be checked: `some` looks only at identified individuals, so only open_pct is tested.
The SOP does not say whose match this covers. The rule applies it to the entity and to the identified individuals, the same subjects as 4.1.
The materiality bar is part of the meaning of the adverse_media and entity_adverse_media facts. The sentence about recording searches has no outcome; see `needs`.
The SOP's industry words are mapped in `maps.industry`. Common ordinary industries are mapped to normal so they are not unknown.
